method: Independent all-string semantic and written-form review. All 50 unique source groups were read in each of nine files; all 63 leaves and 11 booleans were structurally checked, and repeated-source consistency was verified. No MT or external translation API was used.

findings.before: Ko tendatee noñemboheraguapýi ko IP kundaharápe.
findings.after: Ko tendatee noñemboheraguapýi ko IP kundaharapépe.
findings.assessment: The original inflected kundahára (browser) rather than retaining kundaharape (address). Restored the complete address stem before the locative suffix so domain registration refers to the IP address.
The title is a passive result, Access Denied. Added the participle stress accent in the Curaçao/Bonaire orthography; the finite/base verb spelling nenga is used in other grammatical contexts.

languageAssessments.notes: Distinct Papiamentu in Curaçao/Bonaire spelling. Technical and causal meanings hold; do not automatically call this the Aruba Papiamento profile.
Recognizably Paraguayan Guarani. Technical terminology has published Mozilla support. Review of longer native idiom remains useful; this does not certify coverage of all Bolivian Guarani varieties.
Hawaiian clause structure, ʻokina and kahakō are defensible; technical paraphrases preserve source meaning. Native fluency and conventional server/domain terminology remain review priorities.
Recognizably Seychellois Creole, not Haitian or French with altered spelling. Availability, timeout, origin-server and request semantics are preserved.
South African Sesotho-style orthography and clauses are defensible. Existing unavailable and negative-existential repairs hold. Do not infer a Lesotho-specific orthographic profile.
Distinct Setswana vocabulary/concords. Unavailability now means cannot be used, not nonexistence. Technical loan spelling and regional orthographic preferences can receive further review.

Recognizable Xitsonga with coherent concords. Browser/server loans are understandable. Longer apology and connection-number clauses merit fluent idiom review; no certain meaning correction identified.

Recognizable siSwati morphology and orthography rather than verbatim Zulu. Reviewed source meaning across every string, but independent fluency assessment remains limited; no speculative grammar edits applied.

Distinct Zimbabwean/Northern Ndebele forms such as khathesi, nxa, njalo, -jayele- and le- are present. Broader overlap with Zulu is expected; my idiom confidence is limited, so no unsupported substitutions applied.

sharedNotes: Across several languages best is expressed with a comparative or an emphatic very-well construction. This preserves the practical recommendation to enable JavaScript without changing it into a requirement or a speed claim; a fluent editor can refine superlative idiom if desired.

All pages preserve unavailable versus nonexistent, origin server, elapsed time limit, IP flooding as excessive requests, abnormal connections without claiming attack, and expected rather than guaranteed maintenance return.
No native-speaker sign-off is claimed. All files remain model-authored translations with independent model review.
